To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The memory-less network adapters show practically no performance penalty for the NAS parallel benchmark on 8 processes, 2) The memory-less adapters show a 10% performance degradation for the MPI ping pong and 3) The memory-less adapter show a 10-20% performance degradation for a scatter operation on 8 processes for message size IB-4KB.
memory-less adapters can be used on PCI-Express InfiniBand system and can benefit next-generation InfiniBand interconnects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance analysis of next generation memory-less adapters and the effect of the memory-less adapters on the performance of the NAS parallel benchmarks.
the design and implementation of the third generation Infini-Band adapters and their use in the context of high-performance computing systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for the applications we tested, memoryless adapters are not a problem.
the memory-less adapters can be used for all types of applications.
the memory-less NICs are a viable alternative to the NICs with local memory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for applications that use a lot of I/O, memory-less adapters are a viable alternative to adapters with local NIC memory.
memory-less adapters are a better option than memory-full adapters.
the memory-less network adapters have a negligible performance impact on the end applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for the applications that we tested, the memory-less adapters can be used with no significant performance impact.
the performance of memory-less network adapters is very close to that of network adapters with local NIC memory.
memory-less adapters can be used in next generation systems without any significant performance impact on the applications.
